summary: Courchevel Altiport (CVF/LFLJ) is a legendary mountain airport serving the exclusive Courchevel ski resort in the French Alps, perched at an elevation of approximately 2,008 meters (6,588 feet). It is renowned worldwide for having one of the shortest and steepest runways in commercial aviation, measuring just 537 meters with a gradient of about 18.5%, making it a bucket-list destination for experienced pilots and a featured challenge in flight simulators. The airport primarily handles small private aircraft and ski-season charter flights, with no possibility of a go-around due to the surrounding Alpine terrain.
faqs:
Q: Why is Courchevel Altiport considered one of the most challenging airports in the world?
A: Its extremely short 537-meter runway combined with an 18.5% gradient and surrounding mountainous terrain leaves no room for a go-around, requiring highly skilled pilots with specific mountain landing qualifications.

Q: What types of aircraft can land at Courchevel?
A: Only small turboprop aircraft and light private jets can operate here, with carriers like Alpine Airlines and various charter operators providing seasonal ski-season service.

Q: When is the airport operational?
A: The airport primarily operates during the winter ski season from December to April, though it can handle limited summer traffic as well.

Q: Do I need a special license to fly into Courchevel?
A: Pilots must hold a specific mountain rating and have prior experience with the airfield, as standard commercial licenses are not sufficient for this demanding approach.
transport_tips: Ground transport from the airport to Courchevel's ski villages is typically arranged via the resort's shuttle services or pre-booked private transfers, as the altiport sits between Courchevel 1550 and Courchevel 1850. Helicopter transfers to nearby Chambery or Geneva are a popular alternative for travelers continuing to other destinations. Taxi services are available but should be booked in advance during peak ski season due to high demand.
local_tip: Request a window seat on the left side of the aircraft during approach for a breathtaking view of the snow-capped Alps and the dramatic mountain landing, and bring a camera ready—many passengers describe the steep descent as the most scenic arrival of their lives.
